title: Special Features of Audit of Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)
outcomes: Explain NBFCs, registration and scale-based regulation.
Apply prudential norms on capital, income recognition and provisioning.
Perform audit procedures and report to RBI and under CARO.
Apply Ind AS and Division III presentation.

meta.exam_tip: Quote the 90-day glide path date and the scale-based layer in NBFC cases.

concepts.title: NBFCs, registration and scale-based regulation
body: NBFCs are companies registered under the Companies Act engaged mainly in lending, investing in securities, leasing, hire purchase and similar financial activities (excluding agriculture, industrial and real estate businesses as principal activities). The principal business test: financial assets over 50% of total assets and financial income over 50% of gross income.

Registration with RBI under section 45-IA of the RBI Act requires a minimum net owned fund, being raised in phases from ₹2 crore to ₹10 crore for most existing NBFCs by 31 March 2027; P2P lenders, account aggregators and NBFCs without public funds or customer interface stay at ₹2 crore, while IFCs and IDF-NBFCs need ₹300 crore.

Scale-based regulation classifies NBFCs into base, middle, upper and top layers by size and risk, with stricter capital, governance and prudential norms as layers rise. Banks and NBFCs differ in deposits (NBFCs cannot accept demand deposits), payment systems and deposit insurance.
concepts.analogy: NBFCs are lenders without bank licences, regulated by layer.
concepts.work: An NBFC cannot issue cheques drawn on itself like a bank.

concepts.title: Prudential norms: capital, income recognition and provisioning
body: Capital requirements: deposit-taking and middle/upper layer NBFCs maintain minimum capital ratios (e.g. CRAR of 15% with Tier 1 at least 10% for applicable NBFCs).

Income recognition: income on NPAs is recognised only on realisation. NPA norms historically used 180 days; RBI's glide path moved NBFCs to 90 days in stages (150 days by March 2024, 120 days by March 2025, 90 days by March 2026).

Provisioning follows asset classification (standard, substandard, doubtful, loss) under RBI directions for NBFCs not on Ind AS; Ind AS NBFCs use expected credit loss, with a prudential floor comparison under RBI's Ind AS guidance.
concepts.analogy: Same IRAC logic as banks, with NBFC-specific timelines.
concepts.work: From March 2026, NBFCs classify loans overdue beyond 90 days as NPAs.

concepts.title: Audit procedures, frauds and auditor's duties
body: Audit procedures: verify registration and NOF; compliance with prudential norms; loan sanction, disbursement, documentation, security and classification; investments and valuation; borrowings and asset-liability mismatch; and related party exposures.
Frauds in NBFCs are classified and reported to RBI under its directions; auditors report frauds as required by the Companies Act and RBI.

Auditor's duties: report under the RBI's NBFC Auditor's Report Directions (registration, NOF, prudential compliance, public deposits), CARO 2020 clauses (including whether registration is required), RBI rules on appointment of statutory auditors (eligibility, tenure, rotation) and certification of supervisory returns.
concepts.analogy: NBFC auditors report to shareholders and to RBI.
concepts.work: An auditor must report to RBI if an NBFC accepts public deposits without permission.

concepts.title: Ind AS and Schedule III Division III for NBFCs
body: Ind AS applies to NBFCs in phases based on net worth and listing; their statements follow Division III of Schedule III, which differs from Division II (e.g. liquidity-based order — financial assets first; specific line items for loans, investments, derivatives).
Related party exposure disclosures and other RBI-prescribed disclosures accompany Ind AS statements.
Auditors check Ind AS 109 classification, ECL models, fair values and Division III presentation.
concepts.analogy: NBFC statements follow Division III with financial items first.
concepts.work: An NBFC's balance sheet starts with cash and loans, not PPE.

illustrations.title: NPA timing for an NBFC loan
illustrations.q: An NBFC in the base layer has a loan with an instalment overdue by 91 days at 31 March 2026. Under RBI's glide path, NBFCs must move to the 90-day NPA norm by 31 March 2026. Is the loan an NPA? Also state the minimum net owned fund most NBFCs need after the phase-in.

checks.label: Minimum NOF for most NBFCs after the phase-in (₹ crore)

illustrations.title: Is it an NBFC?
illustrations.q: A company's financial assets are 55% of total assets and income from financial assets is 60% of gross income. Another company's figures are 40% and 70%. Which needs NBFC registration under the principal business criteria?

jobs.title: Statutory audit of a middle-layer NBFC
jobs.situation: A ₹3,000 crore vehicle finance NBFC on Ind AS.
steps: Check registration, layer and capital compliance.
Test loan classification against the 90-day norm.
Review ECL model and prudential floor.
Report under RBI directions and CARO.
jobs.takeaway: Prudential compliance is as important as the financial statements.

mcqs.q: The principal business test for NBFCs uses the threshold:
options: Fifty percent of assets and fifty percent of income

mcqs.explain: Key difference from banks. In practice: no cheque facility.

mcqs.q: RBI's scale-based regulation divides NBFCs into:
options: Base, middle, upper and top layers
mcqs.explain: Four layers. In practice: top expected empty.

mcqs.q: Under the glide path, NBFCs adopt the 90-day NPA norm by:
mcqs.explain: Staged from 180 days. In practice: check NBFC category.
mcqs.topic: Prudential norms: capital, income recognition and provisioning

mcqs.q: Income on NPAs of NBFCs is recognised:
mcqs.explain: Prudential norm. In practice: reverse unrealised.
mcqs.topic: Prudential norms: capital, income recognition and provisioning

mcqs.q: Ind AS NBFCs present statements under:
mcqs.explain: NBFC format. In practice: liquidity order.
mcqs.topic: Ind AS and Schedule III Division III for NBFCs

mcqs.q: NBFC auditors report specific matters to RBI under:
mcqs.explain: RBI directions. In practice: separate report.
mcqs.topic: Audit procedures, frauds and auditor's duties

mcqs.q: Minimum NOF for most NBFCs after the phase-in is:
mcqs.explain: Raised from ₹2 crore with exceptions. In practice: check timeline.

checks.label: Minimum NOF for most NBFCs after the phase-in (₹ crore)

model.title: Principal business test

summary: NOF moving from ₹2 crore to ₹10 crore.
RBI auditor report directions; Division III.
traps: Applying the old 180-day norm after March 2026.

viva.q: What is the principal business test?
viva.model: Financial assets above half of total assets and financial income above half of gross income.

viva.q: Name the layers under scale-based regulation.
viva.model: Base layer, middle layer, upper layer and top layer.

viva.q: Describe the NPA glide path for NBFCs.
viva.model: From 180 days to 150 days by March 2024, 120 days by March 2025 and 90 days by March 2026.

viva.q: What does the NBFC auditor report to RBI?
viva.model: Matters like registration, net owned fund, compliance with prudential norms and acceptance of public deposits.

viva.q: How does Division III differ from Division II?
viva.model: It presents items in order of liquidity with financial assets first and NBFC-specific line items.

cases.title: LendEasy P2P Ltd.
cases.case: LendEasy is a peer-to-peer lending NBFC in the base layer. It accepted ₹2 crore from the public as deposits to fund loans. Several borrower loans were overdue 100 days at 31 March 2026. It prepares Ind AS statements.

mcqs.q: Accepting public deposits without RBI permission must be:
options: Reported by the auditor to RBI
mcqs.explain: RBI directions. In practice: serious breach.
mcqs.topic: Audit procedures, frauds and auditor's duties

mcqs.q: Loans overdue 100 days at 31 March 2026 are:
mcqs.explain: Glide path reached 90 days. In practice: reverse income.
mcqs.topic: Prudential norms: capital, income recognition and provisioning

mcqs.explain: Ind AS NBFC format. In practice: ECL.
mcqs.topic: Ind AS and Schedule III Division III for NBFCs

mcqs.q: P2P NBFCs fall in which layer?
mcqs.explain: As per scale-based regulation. In practice: lighter norms.
